programme.title: Quentin Blake: The Drawing of My Life
programme.desc: Quentin Blake turns 89 in December 2021. His first book was published 61 years ago, and over 500 volumes later, he is still hard at work, drawing every day and determined to break down the barriers between illustration and `fine arts'. Blake shares his pleasure in the blank page, the scratch of a quill, and the enjoyable mischief and chaos of childhood.

programme.title: Play for Today
programme.desc: Their Morris packed to the gills, the punctilious Keith and the more spontaneous Candice-Marie arrive at a Dorset campground for ten nights of idyllic bliss. It starts off pretty perfect, it's peaceful, they go sightseeing, eat vegetarian food and go in search of raw milk. Then a fellow with a loud radio pitches his tent near theirs. Things get worse when a couple arrive on a motorcycle, make noisy love in their tent and start an illegal campfire.

programme.title: The Last Battle of the Vikings
programme.desc: Marine archeologist Dr Jon Henderson tells the incredible story of the Norsemen in Scotland. Visiting fascinating archeological sites across Scotland and Norway, he reveals that, although the battle at Largs marked the end of an era for the Norsemen, their presence continued to shape the identity and culture of the Scottish nation to the present day.

programme.title: The Hunt for Lady Olive and the German Submarine
programme.desc: Following the search to discover what happened when a secret Royal Navy Q-ship and a German U-boat allegedly sank each other in battle on a fateful February morning in 1917.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: The pub has been the mainstay of British society since medieval times, a cornerstone of any community playing a unique role in national life. A look at the core values of this definitively British institution and whether it can survive.

programme.title: The Witness is a Whale
programme.desc: Archival footage, hidden documents, and personal records reveal one of the greatest environmental crimes of the 20th century: the secret and illegal slaughter of hundreds of thousands of whales by the Soviet Union during the Cold War.

programme.title: The Search for the Lost Manuscript: Julian of Norwich
programme.desc: Medieval art historian Dr Janina Ramirez tells the incredible story of a book hidden for centuries in the shadows of history, the first book ever written in English by a woman, Julian of Norwich, in 1373. Revelations of Divine Love dared to present an alternative vision of man's relationship with God - a theology fundamentally at odds with the church of Julian's time - and for 500 years the book was suppressed.

programme.title: Hidden Wales: Last Chance to Save
programme.desc: Will Millard returns with more of Wales's hidden wonders as he explores some of the country's forgotten historic buildings. From extravagant mansions to a 500-year-old farmhouse, crumbling chapels to a massive military fort, and from spectacular industrial sites to a stunning 19th-century theatre, Will travels the length and breadth of Wales to find some of the most vulnerable old buildings, telling their incredible histories and meeting the passionate individuals who are trying to rescue them.

programme.title: The Cambridgeshire Crucifixion
programme.desc: In 2017, a routine archaeological dig discovered human remains on a housing development. Once the bones are washed back at HQ, the team find a nail through the heel of one of the individuals, a discovery that may be a very rare Roman crucifixion.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds, and Power: The Story of the Village
programme.desc: The village of Milton Abbas in Dorset perfectly captures the romantic notion of the idyllic English village, but as archaeologist Ben Robinson reveals, behind it lurks a history of one man's wealth and power. With help from local historians, Ben learns how the local landowner in the 18th century destroyed a nearby town, uprooting its residents, because it ruined the view from his house. The landscape was transformed and a new village was built as part of his showpiece estate.

programme.title: The Stuarts in Exile

programme.title: Where Eagles Dare
programme.desc: World War II espionage thriller scripted by Alistair MacLean from his bestseller.
